key_insight: Asymmetric supervised contrastive pre-training learned cross-national EHR representations that transferred better than standard supervised or contrastive baselines, especially for few-shot prediction.
clinical_relevance: This could help hospitals reuse large foreign EHR data to improve prediction models when local labeled data are limited or coding systems differ.
method: Pre-trained temporal Transformer encoders on 3.98 million Taiwanese NHIRD patients.
Used Asymmetric SupCon to cluster patients with the same target outcome without forcing negative cases together.
Mapped heterogeneous clinical vocabularies with a hybrid direct-mapping plus embedding-retrieval pipeline before transfer to U.S. datasets.
evidence_signal: In transfer to MIMIC-IV and EHRSHOT, the NHIRD-pretrained models improved over random initialization; under matched pre-training scale, Asymmetric SupCon achieved higher mean AUPRC than direct BCE on all four tasks and beat Standard SupCon on three of four.
watch_item: Cross-site vocabulary mapping and performance gains may not fully generalize to settings with different coding practices, workflows, or outcomes, so external validation is still needed.
paper_title: Bridging the EHR Divide: Asymmetric Contrastive Learning for Cross-National Medical Representation Transfer
